report.summary: Chunk 7 of 7 for daedalus/eval/mint.py: defines save_minted_tasks, add_minted_task, confirm_minted_task. All docstring claims are verifiable against this code except those referencing external functions.
risks: add_minted_task | medium | load_minted_tasks is not defined in this chunk; if it fails or returns unexpected data, the function may raise an error or behave incorrectly. | Verify that load_minted_tasks is defined and returns a list of dicts with 'id' keys.

confirm_minted_task | medium | confirm_task is not defined in this chunk; if it mutates the task in-place, the mutation is persisted via save_minted_tasks. But if confirm_task returns a value or has side effects not visible here, behavior is uncertain. | Verify that confirm_task modifies the dict in-place and does not require the return value.

handoff.purpose: Defines three functions for persisting minted tasks to a JSON store: save_minted_tasks (overwrite), add_minted_task (upsert by id), confirm_minted_task (confirm one task by id and persist).

symbols.name: save_minted_tasks
symbols.note: Writes a JSON file with sorted tasks. Returns the path written.

symbols.name: add_minted_task
symbols.note: Loads existing tasks, upserts by id, and saves. Returns path.

symbols.name: confirm_minted_task
symbols.note: Loads tasks, confirms one task by id via confirm_task, saves, and returns the task or None.

claims.text: Overwrite the mint store with exactly ``tasks``.
claims.why: The function opens the file in write mode and dumps the tasks, replacing any previous content.

claims.text: Deterministic formatting (sorted keys, sorted by id) so the diff is meaningful in review -- same contract as ``harness.write_baseline``.
claims.why: The code sorts tasks by id and uses json.dump with sort_keys=True and indent=2, ensuring deterministic formatting. The reference to harness.write_baseline is outside this chunk.
The function returns the variable p, which is the path used.

claims.text: Persist ``task`` into the mint store, keyed by id.
claims.why: The function loads existing tasks, inserts/overwrites by id, and saves.

claims.text: Idempotent: minting the same diff twice (same target + same must_include, via the content hash in ``_mint_from_diffs``) yields the same id and overwrites in place rather than duplicating -- re-running a mint (e.g. after a rebase that reproduces an identical patch) must not inflate the quarantine count.
claims.why: The idempotency depends on the task id being derived from content (via _mint_from_diffs) which is not in this chunk. The function itself overwrites by id, so if the same id is produced, it will overwrite. The claim about quarantine count refers to external logic.
The function returns the result of save_minted_tasks, which returns the path.

claims.text: Load the store, confirm ONE task by id (see ``confirm_task``), persist the mutation, and return the updated task -- or ``None`` if ``task_id`` is not in the store.
claims.why: The function loads tasks, iterates to find the task by id, calls confirm_task on it (assuming confirm_task mutates in-place), saves, and returns the task. If not found, returns None.

claims.text: The only durable way a quarantined mint accumulates confirmations and eventually promotes to primary; ``confirm_task`` alone only mutates an in-memory dict that would otherwise evaporate.
claims.why: This claim refers to external behavior (promotion to primary, quarantined mint) not present in this chunk. confirm_task is not defined here, so its behavior is unverifiable.

observations.what: save_minted_tasks uses DEFAULT_MINT_STORE_PATH from outside the chunk as default path.
add_minted_task calls load_minted_tasks which is not defined in this chunk.
confirm_minted_task calls confirm_task which is not defined in this chunk.
confirm_minted_task saves the entire tasks list after mutating one task; if confirm_task does not mutate in-place, the mutation is lost.
